card.name: Cha Cha Cha
card.tagline: Playful Cuban dance born from the danzon-mambo.
card.profile: Cha-cha-cha is a Cuban dance and music genre introduced by composer/violinist Enrique Jorrin of the charanga Orquesta America in the early 1950s, developed from the danzon-mambo. Jorrin simplified the syncopation to make the music easier to dance; dancers at Havana's Silver Star Club improvised a triple step whose shuffling sound ('cha-cha-cha') named the genre. The first recordings, 'La enganadora' and 'Silver Star,' were recorded in March 1953 on Panart. The footwork resembles steps in Afro-Cuban Santeria dances. Played by charanga ensembles (English Wikipedia).
card.insight: After the success of 'La enganadora,' cha-cha-cha eclipsed both mambo and danzon as the most popular dance style in Cuba, and by 1955 the craze had spread internationally; it became one of the five International Latin ballroom dances (English Wikipedia).
